interest: Suspected Japanese fortification of the Mandated Islands.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.34562I and related cross-reference records, covering November 1932 to June 1936) documents United States monitoring of Japanese naval facilities, harbor access, and suspected militarization in the western Pacific. It focuses on international rumors and press reports alleging clandestine Japanese submarine base construction and fortifications in the League of Nations South Seas Mandate (specifically the Caroline and Mortlock Islands), alongside Tokyo press assertions that the mandated islands were administered as sovereign territory immune to foreign objections. In addition, the file records diplomatic initiatives regarding reciprocal visits by public vessels like the USS Alden to unopened ports in the mandated islands, as well as a Far Eastern Affairs memorandum detailing strict new port, aviation, and communications regulations instituted by the Kwantung Government at the naval port of Port Arthur.
